Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No

Comments: On 10/12/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 09/26/2023 (IR 3620008, Enforcement 419234).On 09/26/2023, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, and SWMA 301 for the releases of production fluid were issued as outstanding. Violations of 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) were issued for the accelerated erosion and lack of maintenance of the access road. The following was observed during inspection on 10/12/2023:While onsite, I called Paul Stiner of Diversified to discuss the observations regarding the production fluid within the berm and behind tank 5.A relatively small area behind tank 5 yielded some higher readings, but not as high as noted in inspection 3620008 (Photos 1-3). It is recommended to scrape up this area to ensure there are no residual areas of fluid. Between inspections, rain most likely diluted anything remaining.The valve on tank 4 appeared to have been replaced. The ground under the original valve appeared to have been remediated as seen by adequate readings and buckets onsite (Photos 4-7).Adjacent to the valve on tank 4, the lower section of the berm displayed elevated readings (Photos 8-11).The berm overall in this area appeared to require remediation to ensure no areas of elevated conductivity remain both inside and outside of the berm (Photos 12, 13).The access road appeared to remain in poor condition (Photos 14, 15).Due to the observations regarding the elevated conductivity readings and the condition of the access road, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details

Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming

Comments: At time of inspection, 43 degs. and cloudy. There are (5) wells on this pad. They are the Jack 1H, 2H, WYO 3H, WYO 4H and the WYO 5H, all were in production. The (9x5) and the (13x9) annulus vents are plumbed to surface w/ 2" pipe and tied into a 2" common pipe venting to the prod. tank with the exception of the 2H, which is a (2) string well and only has the (9x5) annulus venting to tank, the (20x9) annulus has an open top. All annulus vents are open and venting to production tank with the exception of the WYO 4H (20x13) annulus which has a Sentry valve venting to atmosphere. The cellars had water in them w/ no active bubbling observed during insp. An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. 2/10/23) was turned on to check for gas at Sentry valve, cellars, at the well heads and left on during walk around pad and prod. equipment. No gas was detected in the ambient air. - Individual well pressures listed below were all taken off SCADA gauges: - 1H - prod. tree top press.: 492.3 psi., prod. csg. press.: 601.5 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 1.8 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 1.6 psi., and prod. line press.: 488.3 psi. (OUTST) - 2H - prod. tree top press.: 494.4 psi., prod. csg. press.: 336.8 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 1.5 psi. and prod. line press.: 494 psi. - 3H - prod. tree top press.: 801.1 psi., prod. csg. press.: 800.1 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 1 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 4 psi., and prod. line press.: 482.6 psi. (OUTST) - 4H - prod. tree top press.: 498.1 psi., prod. csg. press.: 560.9 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 0 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 0 psi., (20x13) annulus press.: 1.1 psi. and prod. line press.: 498 psi. (OUTST) - 5H - prod. tree top press.: 482.9 psi., prod. csg. press.: 168.0 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 0 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 1 psi., and prod. line press.: 481 psi. - There is a self contained on site compressor on the pad and running at time of inspection. - There is self contained ancillary equipment on the pad. - No obvious concerns or new violations noted.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/24/2023 to XTO ENERGY INC in Chapman Twp, Clinton county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: XTO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/24/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 996173
Permit API: 035-21217
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Chapman Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/24/2023
Comments: On May 24, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at the XTO Energy PA Tract Pad A access road and Dry Run Rd. On May 9, 2023 XTO reported a spill of production fluid from a tanker truck at the XTO Energy PA Tract Pad A but, the spill occurred on 9 different areas of Dry Run Rd. and the short access road to Well Pad A. The 9 different spill areas have been excavated and backfilled. The DEP screened the excavation areas with a soil conductivity meter. Excavation areas Mile 4, Mile 5.4, Mile 7.3, and Mile 9 still had areas of conductivity over range of DEP's soil conductivity meter. The upper limit of the DEP's soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. The DEP met with XTO's well tender for the area during the inspection. DEP informed him about the areas that were found and he relayed the information to XTO Jason Canose. DEP spoke with Mr. Canose later on the phone and explained the areas that were found to have soil conductivity over range of the soil conductivity meter. Mr. Canose said he was on his way to check the areas and he would be in contact with Moody and Associates to have them delineate the areas missed during the original excavation. I informed the Environmental Cleanups Program of the areas found and they are copied on this inspection report.Violations from Inspection Report 3551489 are still continuing.

Comments: On May 27, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation (CSE) at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows up to IR 4181973, where the violation issued in IR 4088070 was left outstanding for failure to restore the well site by 10/30/2025, in accordance with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was executed between the Department and the operator on December 16, 2021. The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 COA states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites."Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed during the inspection:The former well site appears to overall exhibit approximately 50% vegetative growth during this inspection, although some isolated locations on site remain sparsely vegetated (photos 17 and 18). The temporary stabilization applied on site appears to be adequate at the time of inspection. Erosion control blanketing was installed north of the former well pad in a location that appeared to be prone to receiving high volumes of stormwater flow. The erosion control blanketing appears to have encouraged vegetative growth to take hold in this location (photos 13-15). However, further review is required by the Department to determine if the feature observed in this location is approved, pre-existing, and/or discharges stormwater in a manner that will not result in erosion. Additional apparent third-party vehicle tracks were observed at the former well pad location (photos 7, 20, and 21). The Department recommends that the operator continue to document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, take reasonable efforts to stop them while promoting continued vegetative growth, and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. The portion of the super silt fence located within the site boundaries appears to be repaired and maintained in accordance with current regulations, at the time of inspection (photo 16). The Department recommends that the operator continue to maintain the super silt fence in accordance with manufacturer specifications, while it is in-use during site restoration.No loose sediment was observed in the channel that empties into the Sediment Trap that reportedly pre-exists well site construction (photo 19). Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4088070 shall remain outstanding.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 896406
Permit API: 063-32044
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Grant Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/06/2020
Comments: On 10/6/20 at 0955 hrs., I conducted an inspection of PA General Energy Co., LLC's J Elmer Lockhart 1127 well (API 063-32044) in Grant Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a reported release of brine/production fluid from a vent at the well head. The well was shut-in by the operator on 10/1/20, prior to the release. A well tag is affixed to the well head. A site ID sign with the operator's name, address, phone number, and well permit should be posted pursuant to OGA 3211(G). On 10/5/20, the operator reported a release of brine/production fluid from a vent between casing strings to the Department. The exact amount of fluid released is unknown, but it was initially estimated as a couple of barrels. Upon inspection of the release area, the size of the impacted area appears to be consistent with a multi-barrel release. The fluid impacted an area at the well head, then flowed down an access road to a lower area where the landowner has various junk vehicles staged. At the time of inspection, Huey Brothers had excavated the lower area and access road. Moody & Associates has been contracted as a consultant and was field screening for soil conductivity. PID screening was yielding no readings. On 10/7/20 I received an update from Nathan Harris with PGE stating that the excavation of the lower area was reaching depths of 10-12 feet in spots, due to the released material hitting an area of weathered rock and migrating vertically.The release of production fluid/brine from the well head constitutes violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and CSL 402(b). The violations associated with this release will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release and demonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/09/2023 to NUCOMER ENERGY LLC in Hickory Twp, Forest county. 78a64(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL AND CONDENSATE TANKS - Owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment for a tank or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons to contain oil or condensate produced from a well which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR Part 112.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: NUCOMER ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/09/2023
Violation Code: 78a64(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL AND CONDENSATE TANKS - Owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment for a tank or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons to contain oil or condensate produced from a well which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR Part 112.
Violation ID: 984772
Permit API: 053-30164
Unconventional: Yes
County: Forest
Municipality: Hickory Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/09/2023
Comments: On 02/09/2023, I conducted a routine partial inspection of the secondary containment around the tank battery at Nucomer Energy's DR02 PAD. The Department was informed by TJ Pennino of EMKEY GATHERING that repairs had been made to the tank battery containment. A tape was used to attempt to patch the numerous holes in the liner. Several of the tape patches had water and bubbles coming out of the edges when pressed. Another patch did not properly adhere to the liner material and the edge is curling up as seen in photos #2 and 4. The south corner had numerous small holes repaired. There are still quite a lot of what look to be pinholes present see photos #1 and #5. The gravel on the front side of the containment wasn't cleared off adequately to inspect the liner for more failures. Also, the north corner had previously had a repair attempt made with the extruder tool. The failed extruded patches are still in place. The extruder tool melted through the liner due to the insufficient thickness of the liner.The tank impoundment was holding a small amount of water on the back side when inspecting the repairs, bubbles, and silt was seen "squirting" through the bottom of the containment coming from below the gravel ballast. This indicates the base of the tank containment liner is compromised. Numerous holes are still present on the edges and berms, and holes also in the base of the containment liner recently being found all lead to this recommendation. The liner must meet the permeability requirement of 1 x10^-10 cm/sec. Due to these findings, it is recommended that the secondary containment liner be fully replaced.

Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/08/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 984958
Permit API: 015-20372
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/10/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Lutz 015" Marcellus well site.Mike Mcnett (Repsol) called the DEP on Wednesday February 8, 2023 to report an estimated 10 gallon release of produced liquid from the dumpline onto the pad surface. I spoke with McNett on site. Two days ago Well Services was trying to unload one of the Marcellus wells at this site. When they sent produced liquid from the GPU, a union on the dumpline broke. They immediately stopped the flow, but an estimated 10 gallons leaked onto the pad surface. Immediately after the release, workers removed four 5 gallon buckets full of mostly gravel pad material under the pipe that leaked. Today they are inspecting all the unions on the dumpline. A crew is removing the insulation from the pipe during this inspection. I got electrical conductivity (EC) readings 0.80-1.4 mS/cm from moist soil below the leak. McNett filled a 55 gallon drum with additional impacted pad material during this inspection. EC readings in the pad material after that were 0.21-0.44 mS/cm. Pad material outside of the spill area has EC of 0.10-0.33.Violations cited to the 015-20372 permit are considered immediately corrected.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.08-0.57 mS/cm with an Oakton PCST 5. Air temp 42FJLP

Comments: This site located west off Greeley Road north of junction with Francis Road in a forested area. Tank battery, two brine tanks and one oil tank in secondary containment, located along the access road. Marshall Wurst found this tank battery with a lined secondary containment containing a release of 2-3 bbls of crude oil on 8/23/2019. WQS Taylor inspected this site on 8/28/2019 and issued an NOV to Coastal Petro Corp. for the release of crude oil into the lined secondary containment. There was 1 1/2'-2' of crude oil/water in the secondary containment at the time of initial inspection. A follow-up inspection found that the liquid crude oil/water mix that was in the secondary containment has been removed. There is ice and snow covering most of the bottom of the secondary containment making it unclear as to the extent of the clean-up however the ice around the tanks appears to be clear and does not contain any residual oil contamination. An empty plastic 200 gallon is set in the secondary containment between the oil tank and first brine tank. A follow-up inspection will be completed when there is a thaw and the stone in the secondary containment can be inspected for contamination. This well to be transferred from Coastal Petro Corp. to Titusville Oil & Gas Associates Inc., application for the transfer of wells was sent in on 11/18/2019. Titusville Oil & Gas Associates, Inc. is to complete the clean-up at this site.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2026
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8276968
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/04/2026
Comments: On 06/03/2026 at 0017 hours the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received a notification of a release at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County (CTS #398207). Representative Ralph Babcock stated "on 6/2/26 at 5:15 p.m., a Keystone Clear Water truck driver was loading production water when the line split releasing 25 gallons of produced water. Approximately 10 gallons of produced water spilled into a containment structure while the remaining 15 gallons of produced water spilled onto the ground. Keystone Clearwater vacuumed produced water from the containment structure and scraped up impacted soil for later disposal.The DEP contacted Repsol and spoke with Mr. Babcock at 1145 hours. He stated the material from the release had been recovered and placed in drums onsite. He stated the release took place in the off-loading area of the pad. He stated he was notified of the released at 2345 hours (06/02).On 06/04/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection. I arrived at 0915 hours and met with Mr. Babcock. Environmental Resources was onsite to collect samples from the release and the prior release (CTS#396090). The area of the release was ~33 feet long (photo #2). There were no pooled fluids in the area of the release. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 452-1042 us/cm. The cause of the release was due to a valve malfunction (photo #3). Environmental resources screened the soil in the area of the release and received readings of 1-1.3 mS/cm (1000-1300 us/cm). The recovered material was observed in drums onsite and held within secondary containment (photo #4).The DEP screened the area of the prior release (CTS #396090). Fluids within the stormwater ditch at the release point were field measured for EC at ~452 us/cm. Mr. Babcock stated that this week there would be more material removed from the stormwater ditch at the release point due to elevated soil readings. There was dead vegetation observed downgrade of the affected bio-retention basin (photo #15-16). Fluids within and directly upgrade of the furthest downgrade sump pump were measured for EC between 1.248-2.24 mS/cm (1248-2240 us/cm) (photo #17 and 18). Fluids downgrade of the sump pump were field measured for EC between 173.7-398 us/cm. The violations related to the recent spill (CTS #398207) are considered immediately corrected however, outstanding violations remain open for API#015-23994 from the previous release (CTS #396090).I departed at 1120 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/29/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 959038
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/09/2022
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of an estimated 5 barrels of produced water occurred which then overflowed secondary containment during completion operations on Pad B. I met with Rick Hall of EQT upon arriving on location. According to Mr. Hall, a hose failed which was hooked up to a booster pump that was being used for coiled tubing operations at the time of the release. After the secondary containment overflowed, the produced water flowed toward the stormwater channel along the pad edge. Mr. Hall said that he would have a sump dug in the stormwater channel at the pad edge to attempt to recover as much of the release as possible. Due to the amount of equipment on the pad and the waterlines and electrical cables along the side of the pad, Hall said that little excavation would be possible until completion operations were finished. He said that completions may be done as soon as the middle of July. He also said that Creston Environmental was en route to conduct screening of the site. Due to the volume of fluid which was released from the failed hose and the unknown volume of fluid released to the pad surface, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations remain outstanding for the March 29, 2022 release on Pad B.

He said that completions may be done as soon as the middle of July. He also said that Creston Environmental was en route to conduct screening of the site. Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/27/2022
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on Pad B following a report from the operator of a release of 140 barrels to secondary containment which overflowed the containment on 6/24/2022. I met with company men Mike Hood and Yadir Lozano upon arriving on location They both accompanied me on this inspection. They showed me the location on the pad where the blender had released produced water to the secondary containment. They also showed me the flow path that the release took once it had overflowed containment. The release flowed to the north where it entered the stormwater channel along the northern side of the pad. It then flowed both west and east to both ends of the stormwater channel. The area around the northwest corner of the pad, where the stormwater channel begins, was dry at the time of this inspection. Fluid was observed seeping out of the gravel along the pad edge and into the north stormwater channel. A puddle in the stormwater channel had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 2.10 mS/cm near where these fluid seeps were observed. According to the company men, the release also flowed west over the pad surface and it flowed into the area that had been impacted by the release from 6/9/22. The EC of the fluid on the pad in this area was 4.08 mS/cm. Fluid was observed at the northeast corner of the pad where the north stormwater channel lets out. An EC reading of this fluid could not be taken due to the presence of a rattlesnake in the rocks in that area. On the pad surface near the northeast corner of the pad, I also found puddles with an EC of approximately 2 mS/cm. I recommended to the company men that these puddles be vacuumed up in addition to the other puddles present on the pad and in the north stormwater channel. I also observed a puddle of an oily substance with a green tint in the travel lane along the southern side of the pad. Company man Yadir Lozano said that this had been found just prior to my arrival on location and that they would excavate the impacted gravel material right away. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment. The tanks and containment appear to be in good condition. No issues noted on Pad A.Violations remain outstanding from the release on 6/24/22.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/25/2025 to KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC in East Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8226731
Permit API: 129-26623
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: East Huntingdon Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2025
Comments: On March 25, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the Wissinger 001 Well in regards to an incident reported to the Department at 10:25 am of an explosion at the well site. Present during the inspection were several representatives from Kriebel including Shane Kriebel, Jay Niehenke, Ronald Seich, Josh Hosteler, Nello Fossi, Ben Dicken, and Charles Reaggle (DEP).-This is inspection 1 of a 2 part inspection-Upon arriving onsite the Department spoke to Shane Kriebel. Mr. Kriebel stated that an explosion of the production tank had occurred while the well tender was blowing out the well, at approximately 9:40 am. Mr. Kriebel stated they believe the explosion was caused by a faulty or damaged grounding wire. He stated that approximately 10 barrels of an oil and brine mixture was released. He stated that remediation was underway and that they would be following Act 2 for this clean up. He stated that saw dust and roughly 4 bags of Oil Gator were used to soak up any standing and pooled brine/oil in order to prevent further leaching in to the ground and easier excavation. He stated they had installed booms in the ditch behind the well site to prevent further migration of the released oil and brine.The Department's observations are as follows:At the time of the Department's arrival, the Department observed an area roughly 40 feet around the production equipment that appeared heavily saturated with an orange tinted fluid, presumably an oil and brine mixture. The Department observed what appeared to be the bottom portion of the production tank on the ground near the rest of the production equipment. A light-colored powder(Oil Gator) was observed placed on the ground in the area where the production tank previously was. A ditch that extended along the western perimeter of the well site, and down slope near the southern perimeter was observed. There appeared to be released fluid in this ditch directly behind the production equipment area, as well as in the ditch downslope on the southern perimeter totaling roughly 120 feet of ditch that appeared to be impacted. 2 booms and hay bales were observed installed in the ditch, one approximately 25 feet north of the production equipment, and one approximately 70 feet downslope south of the production equipment.The Department then began to obtain conductivity readings in the area surrounding the production equipment as well as in the ditch. Conductivity readings in the area surrounding the production equipment were OR (over of detectable range, over 20mS), in approximately a 25 foot radius in which readings then appeared to be comparable to background readings of 0.16mS. Conductivity readings in the ditch were also OR, however readings appear to become comparable to the background reading near the northern boom installed with a reading taken at the boom of 0.19mS. Readings at the southern boom installed were OR, with readings taken approximately 15 feet downslope of the southern boom of 13.23mS. The Department recommended to Mr.Kriebel that additional measures be taken to prevent the migration of contaminates downslope. Mr. Kriebel then had an additional boom installed downslope of the previously installed one on the southern perimeter.

Violation ID: 8169733
Permit API: 129-27066
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/27/2023
Comments: December 27 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to the spill reported to the Department on 10/20/2023 (CTS: 375673). According to the operator, the spill was approximately 40 barrels of production fluid, released from the valve near the bottom of the production tank. The initial inspection of the spill is documented in IR 3636824. The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the production tank appeared to be removed from the site and it appeared that excavation of the contaminated material had begun. The area of excavation was approximately 30 feet by 30 feet and roughly 5.5 feet in depth. The Department took conductivity readings at the bottom of the excavated area with readings of 0.02mS, 0.12mS, and 0.18mS. It appeared that all of the excavated material was still on site, in several piles surrounding the excavated hole. In some areas, it appeared sediment had begun to travel downslope from the piles. Upon further inspection, it appeared that no E and S BMPs were implemented anywhere on the site. The Department recommends the operator promptly install E and S BMPs to prevent further migration of sediment and to minimize the potential for further sedimentation to occur.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to implement E and S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Previous violations associated with the release remain outstanding.

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 990918

Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/06/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/6/2023 at 1430 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Blackhill. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #371191 is tied to this release within CTS. On 4/6/2023 at ~1300 hours an initial estimate of 4 barrels of produced water was discovered by Blackhill Energy to have been released from the produced water offload area at the Jackson pad. Prior to my arrival, the estimate was increased to a potential 7 barrels of produced water. The release occurred when the offload valve for the produced water tanks was not closed all the way after offloading. The valve is held in a yellow bin and the produced water was discovered to be leaking from the bin shown in photo #2. As it leaked from the bin, part of the release was contained to secondary containment and part of the release was spilled to the pad surface. During my inspection, fluids located on the pad surface in the known impacted area from the release were field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photos #1 and 2). After inspecting the rock-lined conveyance channel located just west of the release area (photo #4) it was discovered that elevated conductivity fluids were located in the channel. I field measured fluids in the rock-lined conveyance channel along the entirety of the southern edge of the pad. All fluids in the rock-lined channel up to the stormwater control basin were field measured at >19.99mS/cm. Fluid flowing in the rock-lined channel was observed entering the stormwater control basin. I collected a sample (0983-377) for standard analysis code 942 from the fluid located in the rock-lined conveyance channel just before entering the stormwater control basin (photo #11). This fluid was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (photo #10). Two sumps were constructed along the rock-lined channel to begin collecting any fluids flowing in the channel. The DEP requested that the now impacted stormwater contained in the stormwater basin be collected as a regulated substance due to the release impacting it. As I departed a crew were working on excavating the impacted pad material near the point of release and recovering the fluids that were on the surface of the pad. Temporary storage containers were scheduled to be brought in to be staged onsite for storage of the stormwater control basin's water. Plans to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment to begin excavating beneath it were also being made. The drain pipe of the stormwater basin was believed to be clogged but was also closed as a precaution. I departed the site at 1600 hours. Based on the reported release of produced water outside of containment and the discovery of the release entering conveyance channels and reaching the stormwater controls, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23733: 25 Pa.
